mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand in the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity and related sectors.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where housing starts increased over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies are likely to increase investments to meet growing demand.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production declined by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals increased consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the positive economic signal.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where real personal consumption expenditures increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a single month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies are likely to increase investments to meet growing demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increased by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate monetary tightening and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate was above 2% and the consumer price index increased by more than 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% month-over-month and the GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter, it signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased corporate earnings and economic activity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% month-over-month and GDPC1 increases > 0.5% quarter-over-quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increased by more than 1% month-over-month and GDP grew by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter.
